text.p: AT&T Corp announced on Thursday a staff reorganisation intended to focus the company more sharply on meeting customer needs.
"Cutting costs, important as it is, is not the biggest point," said chief operating officer John Walter.
Several hundred mainly management jobs will go, though most staff will be redeployed internally.

The goal is to increase the focus on customer needs, strengthen the use of the AT&T brand, improve "operational excellence," and provide clear accountability for strategic planning and innovation, according to the memo read to Reuters.
The job cuts are linked to the 17,000 that AT&T is cutting over a three-year period in a plan announced at the beginning of 1996. The company has cut 5,700 jobs so far under that plan.
One element of the reorganisation is the integration of advertising, direct mail, sales promotion and sponsorship under a single team to boost AT&T's brand name in the United States.
"It is a reorganisation that was announced internally to employees this afternoon," an AT&T spokeswoman said.
In addition, John Walter, who is to take over from Robert Allen as chief executive in 1998, will look closely at reducing the costly role of consultants within AT&T.
